oewn-00799359-v.learner: to say yes to something, or to answer it in a way that shows you are pleased with it.
examples: Mr. Bingley was obliged to be in town the following day, and consequently unable to accept the honour of their invitation.
he had no engagement at all for to-morrow; and her invitation was accepted with alacrity.

oewn-02240906-v.learner: to take something that is given or offered to you, because you are willing to have it.
examples: She accepted the little parcel with a smile and put it in her pocket.

oewn-00688348-v.learner: to think that something is true, or to hold on to it as true.
examples: I accept his account of that evening, though I cannot prove it.

oewn-05828314-n.learner: one detail or point of a thing, usually spoken of after the word 'in'.
examples: My feelings in every respect forbid it.
The world has been deceived in that respect.

oewn-01231366-n.learner: a polite word or act that shows you think well of someone.
examples: I am most thankful that the discovery is made in time for me to pay my respects to him.
you will of course wish to have your humble respects delivered to them, with your grateful thanks for their kindness

oewn-06216535-n.learner: a way of thinking about someone in which you admire them and think highly of them.
examples: Her respect for him grew as she learned what he had quietly done.

oewn-14442568-n.learner: the state of being joined or tied to something else.
examples: Something, he supposed, might be attributed to his connection with them.
Every kind of pride must revolt from the connection.

oewn-09975626-n.learner: a person with power or influence whom you are joined to in some way, such as by family or friendship; the word is usually used in the plural.
examples: they may wish him to marry a girl who has all the importance of money, great connections, and pride

oewn-13813601-n.learner: a link between two things or events, as when one causes the other or the two share something.
examples: She could see no connection between the letter and his sudden silence.

oewn-13833030-n.learner: the part that is left after other parts have been taken away.
examples: spent the rest of the evening in walking about the room, speaking occasionally to one of his own party
The rest of the evening brought her little amusement.

oewn-01066072-n.learner: being free from work, from strain, or from duty.
examples: He had no rest from his duties from morning until night.

oewn-15299060-n.learner: a short break in what you are doing, so that you can relax.
examples: They stopped halfway up the hill for a rest.

oewn-00955090-v.learner: to tell what happened, giving an account of it.
examples: Elizabeth related to Jane what she had seen pass between the two gentlemen.
she related the particulars of all the pecuniary transactions in which they had been connected

oewn-02681865-v.learner: to have to do with something; to be about it.
examples: Her question relates to the second half of the letter.

oewn-00715072-v.learner: to join two things in your mind by reason or by cause.
examples: He could not relate her sudden coldness to anything he had said.

oewn-01559809-a.learner: not as much in amount or degree.
examples: Her mind was less difficult to develope.
she said less of her astonishment than of her earnest desire for their happiness
The whole journey took less than three hours.

oewn-02355910-s.learner: lower in quality; usually used after the word 'no'.
examples: She would take nothing less than his best work.

oewn-01548893-v.learner: to be on your feet with your body upright.
examples: after standing a few moments without saying a word, he suddenly recollected himself, and took leave

oewn-02617408-v.learner: to be in the state or condition that is named.
examples: his visits to his aunt, of whose good opinion and judgment he stands much in awe

oewn-00670017-v.learner: to bear something or someone unpleasant.
examples: I cannot stand his rudeness any longer.

oewn-07211342-n.learner: a sentence that asks something and calls for an answer.
examples: You may ask questions which I shall not choose to answer.
He repeated the question, with some surprise at her silence.

oewn-07208256-n.learner: one time when somebody asks something.
examples: There was a question from the back of the room about the cost.

oewn-06796625-n.learner: the subject that is being talked about or decided.
examples: The question of her marriage was settled at last.
as a step towards conversing with her himself, attended to her conversation with others
was incapable of attending to the sense of the one before her eyes

oewn-02618797-v.learner: to be there at something such as a meeting, a church service, or a school.
examples: Mr. Darcy was punctual in his return, and, as Lydia informed you, attended the wedding.

oewn-02722442-v.learner: to come along with something as one of the things around it, or to follow it as a result.
examples: Elizabeth had only to suffer from the uncomfortable feelings necessarily attending it

oewn-01440837-a.learner: lasting more time than usual, or lasting the amount of time that is named.
examples: the period of anxiety and fretfulness on her side be as long as it could
How long has she been such a favourite?

oewn-01436368-a.learner: reaching further from one end to the other than usual, or reaching the distance that is named.
examples: They walked down a long road to the church.
She looked out through the long windows at the lawn.
